plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.description: Tiny cream-white flowers fade as the petal-like sepals swell into bright rosy-red bracts. Whole hillsides and garden shrubs end up looking as if they are decked in festive crimson.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January)
plants.location: Coastal bushland and sandstone gullies of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The colorful 'flowers' people admire are mostly enlarged sepals, not petals. They deepen from pink to red after the true flowers have dropped, and that is why the plant is a popular Australian Christmas decoration.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, leafless stems hold rounded clusters of blue, bell-shaped flowers high above strappy, evergreen foliage. They sway like lanterns through the summer heat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer (about November to March), peaking in December and January
plants.location: Coastal regions of South Africa, especially the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'. Despite the common name, it is not a true lily and belongs to the amaryllis family.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: Nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens open in the dead of winter. They sit above leathery, dark-green evergreen leaves and are sometimes dusted with frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter. It blooms around Christmas in mild-winter regions and as late as February or March in colder ones.
plants.location: Mild-winter parts of Europe, including the woodlands and gardens of the Alps and their foothills
plants.funFact: Folklore says this flower sprang from the tears of a girl who had no gift to bring the Christ child. Every part of the plant is toxic, so it was historically used with great caution.
